title: Canonical finite-coefficient structural maps commute with shifts
statement:
Fix a finite field $k_0$ of characteristic $p$, its algebraic closure $k$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and uniformizer $\varpi_E$, and $n\ge1$. Put $A=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. These are the finite coefficient conventions of [def-trf-coefficient-conventions]. Let $X,Y,Z$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and $f:X\to Y$, $g:Y\to Z$ separated finite-type morphisms [def-weil-scheme-morphism-properties]. Use the constant-$A$ module derived categories on their small pro-etale sites, the operations of [def-fix-six-functor-datum], and the compactification-independent $Rf_!$ of [def-compact-support-direct-image-detailed]. Statements about compactification comparisons and composition are on bounded constructible complexes with their bounded-below etale-origin witnesses [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory], as in [thm-sf-comp-composition]; they assert nothing on arbitrary pro-etale complexes. Use the canonical derived shift isomorphisms for $Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!$, the composite shift for composite functors, with the constant-$A$ derived operations of [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and the bounded constructible categories of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility].

The following canonical natural transformations commute with the shift $[1]$:

(1) For proper $f$, the unit $\eta_f:\mathrm{id}\to Rf_*Lf^*$ of the ordinary derived adjunction, on $D^b_c(Y,A)$.

(2) For proper $f$, the canonical proper-coincidence comparison $p_f:Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_*$ specified by the compactification $(\mathrm{id}_X,f)$, on $D^b_c(X,A)$.

(3) The canonical compact-support composition isomorphism $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ of [thm-sf-comp-composition], on the stated bounded constructible etale-origin domain.

(4) The counit $\varepsilon_f:Rf_!Rf^!\to\mathrm{id}$ of the constructible adjunction $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$ of [def-trf-admissibility], on $D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Here $Rf^!=\nu_X^*f^{\times}R\nu_{Y,*}$ is the constructible exceptional inverse image of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image], for the compactification $X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}Y$ used to define it, with $\nu_X,\nu_Y$ the comparison morphisms [def-weil-pbc-site-comparison-morphism]. It carries the composite shift of this formula: $\nu_X^*$ and $R\nu_{Y,*}$ have their canonical derived shifts, and the etale right adjoint $f^{\times}$ has the shift adjoint to the canonical shift of the etale compact-support functor $Rp_{\mathrm{et},*}j^{\mathrm{et}}_!$. Thus, with $\mathrm{id}$ carrying the identity shift, $\varepsilon_f$ is compatible with the canonical shifts, not merely with a shift of $Rf^!$ chosen to make it so.

Precisely, if $\tau:F\to G$ is any transformation in (1)--(4) and $\chi_F(M):F(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}F(M)[1]$, $\chi_G(M):G(M[1])\xrightarrow{\sim}G(M)[1]$ are the specified shift comparisons, then
$$\chi_G(M)\circ\tau_{M[1]}=\tau_M[1]\circ\chi_F(M).$$
The inverses of the two isomorphisms in (2)--(3) satisfy the same equation with source and target interchanged. Shifts and triangulated categories have the conventions of [def-weil-triangulated-category].

source.place: Tags 05SU (lemma-derived-shift), 0DVC (lemma-pre-derived-adjoint-functors), 0A8D (lemma-adjoint-is-exact, shift of a right adjoint, for clause (4)); for the canonical compact-support compositor, literature/stacks-project/more-etale.tex, Tags 0F7B (lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, representative-level map) and 0F7J (lemma-shriek-composition, four-line construction). The combined pro-etale finite-coefficient compatibility assertion is assembled by an agent, not a verbatim Stacks theorem; it supplies the shift-compatibility sentence of the blueprint proof.

proof.text: Fix the shift convention $(K[1])^r=K^{r+1}$, $d_{K[1]}=-d_K$. All pullbacks below use the specified constant-ring identifications. For pro-etale geometric pullback these identifications are isomorphisms by [prop-weil-pbc-proetale-constant-ring-map], and [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations] identifies $Lu^*$ with exact termwise module inverse image. For etale geometric pullback use [prop-weil-pbc-inverse-image-modules-exact]; for $H_T=\nu_T^*$ use [lem-sf-comparison-pullback-exact]. Thus their shift comparisons are the degreewise identities of [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-derived-factorization]. For any right derived functor computed by K-injectives, a resolution $s:K\to I$ can be replaced for $K[1]$ by $s[1]:K[1]\to I[1]$, by [lem-weil-pbc-kinjective-shift]. The resulting degreewise identification $u_*(I[1])=(u_*I)[1]$ is precisely the canonical derived shift: comparison with any other resolving choice is unique in the homotopy category by [lem-sp-kinjective-comparison-principle], and comparison maps also shift. We will use these representatives for calculations, keeping the given canonical shifts.

source.place: lemma-derived-shift; canonical shifts calculated on shifted K-injective resolutions

proof.text: The ordinary derived adjunctions, including $H_T\dashv U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$, are compatible with these shifts. Here is the check rather than an appeal to exactness of the two functors. For an exact module inverse image $L\dashv u_*$, the complex-level transpose is $a\mapsto u_*(a)\eta_M$, with inverse $b\mapsto\varepsilon_I L(b)$, by [lem-weil-pbc-termwise-adjunction-homotopy]. In degree $r$, its transpose at $(M[1],I[1])$ is the same map in degree $r+1$ as at $(M,I)$: the unit and counit have degree zero, and both differentials acquire the same minus sign. The canonical derived Hom bijection is the one characterized by these representatives and resolution comparisons in [lem-pc-pre-derived-adjoint-functors-general]. Shifting those representatives and quasi-isomorphisms therefore preserves that bijection. Apply this to the identity of $LM$: its transpose is the derived unit, so $\chi_{Ru_*L}(M)\eta_{M[1]}=\eta_M[1]$. Apply it to the identity of $Ru_*K$: its inverse transpose is the derived counit, so $\varepsilon_{K[1]}=\varepsilon_K[1]\chi_{LRu_*}(K)$. This proves clause (1) for the given ordinary unit, and also provides both comparison-adjunction equations needed below. The module, rather than merely abelian-sheaf, adjunction is the one used in step 1.

The canonical direct-image composition map $\kappa_{v,u}:R(vu)_*\to Rv_*Ru_*$ commutes with shifts. Indeed [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-pushforward-composition] normalizes it on a K-injective $I$ by $v_*u_*I\xrightarrow{v_*t}v_*J$, where $t:u_*I\to J$ is a K-injective resolution. Use $I[1],J[1],t[1]$ for the shifted input; these are valid resolutions by step 1. The normalized arrow is then $v_*(t[1])=(v_*t)[1]$, which is exactly the required square for the composite shifts. For exact open extension on either site, sheaf-level composition, identity, and site-comparison maps also commute with shifts after termwise descent: their degree-$r$ component on $K[1]$ is their degree-$(r+1)$ component on $K$, and additivity gives the same negative differentials. For pro-etale open extension, exactness is [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-exact]; its composition map is obtained by transposing the identity $(j_2j_1)^*=j_1^*j_2^*$ under [lem-weil-extension-by-zero-adjunction]. For etale open-extension exactness use [lem-weil-pbc-extension-by-zero-exact], and for its composition use [lem-cbc-extension-zero-composition]. The cross-site open comparison is [lem-cbc-proetale-extension-zero-comparison]. In every case the two sides of the shift square are thus the same degree-zero chain map.

source.place: lemma-shriek-composition, direct-image and open-extension composition identifications

proof.text: On the etale site consider a commutative proper/open square with vertical maps $r,p$ proper and horizontal maps $k,i$ open. Its named interchange $\gamma^e:i_!Rr_*\to Rp_*k_!$ has the normalization of [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence]: on a K-injective representative $J$ it is $i_!r_*J\cong p_*k_!J\to p_*I$, for a K-injective resolution $k_!J\to I$. Choose the shifted resolution $k_!J[1]\to I[1]$ for $J[1]$. The sheaf-level proper/open identification is natural in the module, so its degree-$r$ component is the original component in degree $r+1$. The second arrow is the shift of the chosen resolution arrow. Consequently the whole representative is the shifted original arrow, proving the shift square for $\gamma^e$ with the canonical composite shifts. This does not infer shift compatibility from mere naturality. The cited node supplies the normalization and invertibility on $D^+$ for finite $A$; the calculation supplies the extra shift equation. Its special case $r=1$, $k=j_1$, $i=j_2$, $p=u$ is the named etale proper-refinement map.

source.place: lemma-shriek-proper-and-open, first paragraph of proof, and its proper-refinement specialization

proof.text:
For a proper map $u$, the named site direct-image comparison $b_u:H_VRu^e_*\to Ru^p_*H_U$ is the mate specified in [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-direct-image-canonical-mate]. Write $a_u:H_ULu_e^*\to Lu_p^*H_V$ for [lem-weil-pbc-comparison-pullback]. Its module realization comes from the same inverse-image comparison on sheaves, so it commutes with shifts by the degreewise calculation of step 3. Set $q=H_U\varepsilon^e_u\circ a_u^{-1}$. The mate formula is $b_u=Ru^p_*(q)\circ\eta^p_uH_VRu^e_*$. Steps 2 and 3 show that every factor here commutes with shifts. Composition and whiskering preserve the equation by [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker], so $b_u$ does too. Combining $b_p$ with the termwise open comparison $e_j:H_{\overline X}j^e_!\to j^p_!H_X$ gives the named compact-support comparison
$$c_c=Rp^p_*(e_j)\circ b_pj^e_!:H_Y(Rp^e_*j^e_!)\xrightarrow{\sim}(Rp^p_*j^p_!)H_X.$$
Its invertibility on the bounded-below etale-origin domain is [lem-sf-class-compact-support-comparison]. Thus $c_c$ has the shift equation with the specified derived shifts of the candidate, without redefining either shift.

source.place: finite-module site comparisons; counit-mate normalization and termwise open-extension comparison

proof.text:
The named proper-refinement comparison on the pro-etale etale-origin domain has the normalization [lem-sf-proper-open-comparison-site-normalization]
$$\alpha^p_u e_{j_2}=Ru^p_*(e_{j_1})\,b_u j^e_{1!}\,H_{T_2}(\alpha^e_u).$$
Steps 3--5 give the shift equation for every factor on the right and for $e_{j_2}$. Cancel $e_{j_2}$ to obtain it for $\alpha^p_u$ on $H_XL$. For an arbitrary witness $w:H_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, the definition gives $\alpha_u(K,L,w)=Ru_*j_{1!}(w)\circ\alpha^p_{u,L}\circ j_{2!}(w)^{-1}$. The shifted witness is $w'=w[1]\circ\chi_{H_X}(L):H_X(L[1])\to K[1]$. Naturality of the shift comparisons gives $\chi_{Ru_*j_{1!}}(K)\,Ru_*j_{1!}(w')=Ru_*j_{1!}(w)[1]\,\chi_{Ru_*j_{1!}H_X}(L)$ and the corresponding equation for $j_{2!}(w')$. Substitution of these two equations and the square already proved at $L$ cancels $w[1]$ and its inverse, giving the square at $(K,L,w)$. Now [def-sf-refinement-comparison-isomorphism] specifies a candidate comparison $\theta_u$ as $\kappa_{p_2,u}$ followed by $Rp_{2*}(\alpha_u^{-1})$. Both factors commute with shifts. For clarity, if $\chi_G\tau_{[1]}=\tau[1]\chi_F$ and $\tau$ is invertible, multiplying on the left by $\tau[1]^{-1}$ and on the right by $\tau_{[1]}^{-1}$ gives $\chi_F\tau_{[1]}^{-1}=\tau[1]^{-1}\chi_G$; this justifies every inverse used here. Comparisons through common refinements are composites of such arrows by [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed], so they too commute with shifts. For proper $f$, take the compactification $(1_X,f)$: its candidate is $Rf_*1_!$, and the identity-open comparison $1_!\cong1$ is degreewise the identity. Comparing the chosen candidate to this candidate by $\theta$, then using this identity, is exactly the specified $p_f:Rf_!\to Rf_*$ of clause (2). This proves its shift equation and that of its inverse.

source.place: lemma-shriek-proper-and-open and lemma-shriek-composition; proper normalization at the identity-open compactification

proof.text:
Choose compatible compactifications by [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle]: $Y\xrightarrow i\overline Y\xrightarrow sZ$ and $X\xrightarrow a\overline X\xrightarrow p\overline Y$, with $V$, $b$, $q$, $j$ as there; the square $pb=iq$ is Cartesian. The etale compositor on this tower is the specified normalization of [lem-amb-unbounded-compact-support-comparisons]:
$$Rs_*i_!Rq_*j_!\xrightarrow{Rs_*\Gamma_Q j_!}Rs_*Rp_*b_!j_!\xrightarrow{\kappa_{s,p}^{-1}}R(sp)_*b_!j_!\xrightarrow{R(sp)_*\operatorname{comp}_{b,j}}R(sp)_*a_!,$$
where $\Gamma_Q:i_!Rq_*\to Rp_*b_!$ is its proper/open interchange. By the last sentence of the same statement, on bounded-below inputs this $\alpha^e_{g,f}$ is the composition isomorphism of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] with the same normalization; this is the etale compositor used in step 9.

source.place: lemma-shriek-composition, compatible compactification diagram and four-line construction

proof.text: The interchange $\Gamma_Q$ of step 7 is the map of [lem-amb-unbounded-proper-open-interchange] for the square $pb=iq$. Its specified representative on a K-injective $J$, with a K-injective resolution $b_!J\to I$, is $i_!q_*J\cong p_*b_!J\to p_*I$, where the first map is the canonical sheaf proper-support identification (both sides are the same subsheaf of $(iq)_*J=(pb)_*J$). For $J$ representing an object of $D^+$ this is exactly the representative of $\gamma^e_Q$ in [lem-cbc-proper-open-interchange-coherence] used in step 4, so $\Gamma_Q=\gamma^e_Q$ on $D^+$ and the shift calculation of step 4 applies verbatim; its adjoint description is not needed. Hence each of the three arrows of step 7 commutes with shifts, by steps 3--4, and $\kappa_{s,p}^{-1}$ does by the inverse calculation of step 6. The composition and whiskering rule [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] gives the shift square for the etale compositor $\alpha^e_{g,f}$ on $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$.

source.place: lemma-shriek-composition, compatible compactification diagram and four-line construction

proof.text:
Write $c_h:H F_h^e\to P_hH$ for the candidate comparison of step 5. [lem-pur-compact-support-site-coherence] names the same map, $B_h^c=Rp_{p,*}(e_j)\circ\beta_{p,j^e_!}$ with the counit-mate $\beta_p$ and the adjoint open comparison $e_j$, so $B_h=c_h$. Its hypotheses hold here: its datum [def-pur-conventions] is the item's ($k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne p$, $A=A_{E,n}$), the schemes are finite type over $k$, the three maps are separated finite type, and we use the compatible tower of step 7. Its composition identity on $D^+(X_{\mathrm{et}},A)$ reads $c_{gf}H_Z(\alpha^e_{g,f})=\alpha^p_{g,f}H_X\circ(P_gc_f)\circ(c_gF_f^e)$, with $\alpha^e$ the compositor of [lem-amb-etale-compact-comparisons] (step 7) and $\alpha^p$ that of [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Since $c_f$ and $c_g$ are invertible (step 5), this is
$$\alpha^p_{g,f,H_XL}=c_{gf,L}H_Z(\alpha^e_{g,f,L})c_{g,F_f^eL}^{-1}P_g(c_{f,L}^{-1}).$$
Step 8 proves the shift square for the etale middle arrow, and step 5 proves it for each $c_h$. By [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker], and step 6 for inverses, the right side has the shift square with exactly the composite canonical shifts of the statement. This proves it for the named pro-etale compositor on $H_XL$.

source.place: lemma-shriek-composition, compatible compactification diagram and four-line construction

proof.text: For a witness $w:H_XL\xrightarrow{\sim}K$, naturality of the compositor conjugates its value at $H_XL$ by $P_gP_f(w)$ and $P_{gf}(w)$. Use the shifted witness $w[1]\chi_{H_X}(L)$; naturality of both composite shift comparisons cancels those two witness factors just as in step 6. The resulting square is the one at $K$. Choice-independence in [thm-sf-comp-composition] and the cocycle in [prop-compactification-coherence-detailed] conjugate the tower value by the specified refinement comparisons, whose shift squares were proved in step 6. Composition and whiskering preserve the square [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker]. Thus the original $\alpha_{g,f}$ commutes with shifts on the stated domain, and the inverse calculation of step 6 gives its inverse square. This proves clause (3).

source.place: lemma-shriek-composition, compatible compactification diagram and four-line construction

proof.text:
For clause (4), retain the compactification $c=(j,p)$ used in the definition and write $F^e=Rp^e_*j^e_!$, $G^e=f^{\times}$, $P=Rp^p_*j^p_!$, $H_T=\nu_T^*$, $U_T=R\nu_{T,*}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-adjunction-shift-compatibility-unique], the right adjoint $G^e$ of $F^e$ has the unique shift adjoint to that of $F^e$, and its etale counit $\varepsilon^e:F^eG^e\to1$ commutes with these shifts. This is precisely the $G^e$ shift fixed in the statement. The two other factors of $R=H_XG^eU_Y$ carry the canonical shifts of step 1, and the comparison adjunction counit $v_Y:H_YU_Y\to1$ commutes with shifts by step 2. Consequently every factor of the following natural map commutes with shifts:
$$e_M:P H_XG^eU_YM\xrightarrow{c_c(G^eU_YM)^{-1}}H_YF^eG^eU_YM\xrightarrow{H_Y\varepsilon^e_{U_YM}}H_YU_YM\xrightarrow{v_{Y,M}}M.$$
Here $c_c$ is exactly the map of step 5. Applying the composition/whiskering equations from [lem-weil-pbc-commshift-nattrans-comp-whisker] gives
$$e_{M[1]}=e_M[1]\,\chi_{PR}(M).$$
This uses the composite shift of $H_XG^eU_Y$ specified in the question throughout.

source.place: lemma-adjoint-is-exact, adjoint shift construction; explicit composite counit calculation

proof.text:
Identify $e$ with the required constructible counit, including its normalization. By [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin], a bounded constructible $M$ has an etale origin $M\cong H_YN$; by [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude], finite Tor amplitude is preserved and reflected, so $N$ belongs to the etale finite-Tor category when $M$ does. The comparison unit $N\to U_YH_YN$ is an isomorphism by [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison]; by step 2 it is compatible with the canonical shifts, so the quasi-inverse $U_Y$ has the very shift used in step 11. The finite coefficient adjunction and its transport by this unit and $c_c$ are stated in [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons]. The transported counit formula in [det-sp-et-proet-adjunction-transfer] says on $H_YN$ exactly $H_Y\varepsilon^e_N\circ c_c(G^eN)^{-1}$, after the equivalence identifications. To make the equivalence identification explicit, set $t=\eta^\nu_N:N\xrightarrow{\sim}U_YH_YN$. Naturality of $c_c$ and $\varepsilon^e$ gives
$$e_{H_YN}\circ P H_XG^e(t)=v_{Y,H_YN}\circ H_Y(t)\circ H_Y(\varepsilon^e_N)\circ c_c(G^eN)^{-1}=H_Y(\varepsilon^e_N)\circ c_c(G^eN)^{-1},$$
where the last equality is the comparison triangle identity $v_{Y,H_YN}\circ H_Y(t)=1$. The isomorphism $P H_XG^e(t)$ is exactly the source identification from $PH_XG^eN$ to $PH_XG^eU_YH_YN$, so this is the stated transported-counit formula. Thus $e_{H_YN}=\varepsilon_{f,H_YN}$, and naturality along $H_YN\cong M$ gives $e_M=\varepsilon_{f,M}$ for every $M\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,A)$. These are the constructible maps fixed by [def-trf-admissibility]. If its compact-support functor is expressed at another compactification, the refinement comparison of step 6 is inserted on the left, and preserves the equation. This proves clause (4) for the given adjunction and the given shifts.

source.place: finite-coefficient comparison and transported adjunction; compare derived.tex, lemma-adjoint-is-exact

proof.text: All calculations take place on the required domains. The coefficient ring is finite and killed by a power of $\ell$, with $\ell$ invertible on every scheme. The field $k$ is Noetherian because its only ideals are $0$ and $k$; its one-affine spectrum is therefore Noetherian. Finite-type schemes over $k$ and the proper ambient schemes of a compactification are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian] applied first to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and then to the proper maps; the starting schemes are qcqs by [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine], since they are separated finite type over $\operatorname{Spec}k$. Thus the compatible-tower and proper/open comparison hypotheses used above hold. The etale-origin categories are preserved by compact support by [thm-sf-comp-composition]; shifting a witness $H_TN\cong K$ gives $H_T(N[1])\cong K[1]$ by step 1, so every shift equation stays in its domain. Bounded constructible inputs have such witnesses by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin]. For the exceptional counit the preservation and adjunction on finite-Tor constructibles are supplied by [lem-pur-finite-coefficient-adjoint-comparisons], so each term of steps 11--12 is defined there. No assertion about a right adjoint on all pro-etale complexes is needed. Combining the equations proved above gives exactly $\chi_G(M)\tau_{M[1]}=\tau_M[1]\chi_F(M)$ for all four specified transformations. The elementary inverse calculation in step 6 gives the two remaining inverse equations.
